answer: Newcomers join a harbor charter crew. Eight newcomers and one established captain lock a shared $800 bond at the wharf and register one key each. The crew has 30 days to finish 80 verified client jobs, each client-signed and captain-stamped. If one member fakes a job, the whole $800 burns and the crew restarts, so crews vet each other before boarding. A haven that lets strangers wander in alone invites fake fleets. One thousand fakes would need $100,000 in pooled bonds and 10,000 real jobs, about 2,500 hours of work. A wharf full of lone boats is easy to flood; a crewed ship is not.
